transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22
Start: 14:30 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sofia (CSM), Rajiv (Aperture), Emily (Aperture), Dana (Aperture), Tomas (Aperture finance)

Summary (auto): Short retrospective + economic interlock; focus on Feb reliability spike, cost anomaly in embeddings route, and planning pilot constraints for Private VPC deployment.

[00:00] Maya: ok good afternoon everyone thanks for taking the time, uh this is our quarterly interlock, we wanted to go over the usage trends and the surprise in February costs, run through reliability incidents, and then align on next steps for the pilot.
[00:18] Rajiv: Thanks Maya, yep appreciate it. Quick note, we have Dana and Tomás on the call to sign off on any budget changes.
[00:26] Dana: yep hi all, we mostly want to understand the delta vs forecast.
[00:34] Liam: quick intro from my side, I'm Liam, i handle performance for redwood, i'll own the latency bench and the tail-latency analysis.
[00:42] Sofia: and I'm Sofia, i'll be your CSM contact for onboarding and the pilot schedule.
[00:48] Tomás: quick Q up front, do you have a model-level breakdown or just top-level tokens today?
[00:56] Maya: we do have model-level but the spreadsheet we sent was aggregated, we'll send a more granular view after the call.
[01:04] Rajiv: okay cool. so first the usage. we saw a steady 2.3x growth in generation calls month-over-month, embeddings spiked on an internal indexing job in early feb which we didn't plan for.
[01:22] Emily: yeah that was an ML retrain, we inadvertently hashed all records through the embeddings route; that drove a ton of small requests.
[01:31] Maya: so that aligns with the token distribution—lots of short, high-frequency calls which increased per-request overhead. We flagged that in the cost model as non-ideal for our prefix caching.
[01:44] Tomás: can you explain "non-ideal for prefix caching" in lay terms — like why did we pay more?
[01:52] Liam: sure, short version: when you have millions of tiny embedding ops, you lose amortization benefits and RPC cost plus cold cache misses become material.
[02:03] Rajiv: and the KV cache isn't helpful for embeddings because they weren't repeated items, embarrassingly parallel.
[02:11] Maya: right, so two levers: batch the indexing job into larger units, or route it to a cheaper quantized model variant for embeddings.
[02:21] Dana: what does that cheaper variant look like? accuracy tradeoffs?
[02:27] Liam: typically a quantized 8-bit embedder will give ~1-2% nce drop on retrieval metrics but 40-55% cost reduction in throughput. we can show results on your sample set.
[02:43] Emily: that might be ok for background indexing, not for real-time search.
[02:49] Rajiv: Agreed. We'll split indexing vs live queries and keep live on the higher-fidelity model.
[02:56] Maya: ok next, reliability incident review—Feb 12th we saw a 14-minute degradation affecting one region, cause was a node oom after a misconfigured autoscaler policy.
[03:10] Emily: yep we pulled logs, it was a burst of 500 concurrent long-context generation requests that exceeded per-node memory because kv cache grew.
[03:19] Liam: that's a classic sweet spot for continuous batching mis-tuning—runtime kept buffering requests and the KV cache peppered memory. We suggested an autoscaler cap and target per-node kv-slot limits which you adopted on Mar 2nd.
[03:33] Dana: post-fix did tails improve?
[03:36] Liam: p99 improved from 2.3s to 1.2s on similar traffic shapes, p95 pretty stable.
[03:45] Rajiv: ok that helps. question — for our private deployment, how does prewarming work versus hosted?
[03:53] Maya: for Private you get more control — prewarmed nodes and reserved capacity options. you can set instance pre-warm counts and keep a pool for cold-start sensitive routes.
[04:05] Tomás: cost-wise how much does reserved capacity cost vs pay-as-you-go bursts?
[04:10] Maya: we provided a sample committed plan in the pricing deck; at your scale, a 1-year reserved commit typically reduces per-token cost by ~18-28% depending on model mix and utilization. we'll run a tailored calc.
[04:23] Tomás: ok would like that number in time for our April budget meeting.
[04:28] Sofia: we'll add that to next steps — Maya will send the 30-day cost breakdown with a reserved vs burst scenario.
[04:35] Rajiv: Another item — security. we need KMS-integrated key rotation and proof of audit logs for PHI workflows.
[04:44] Maya: we've got KMS integrations and audit log exports, we can share the SOC2 + audit playbook. for PHI we recommend Private with customer-managed KMS/HSM.
[04:55] Emily: is there any difference in how we capture request-level audit trails between hosted and Private?
[05:01] Liam: hosted can stream audit events to your SIEM via secure connector, Private has the same exports but you can keep logs entirely in your VPC.
[05:10] Dana: good. please send the security artifacts.
[05:14] Maya: yes, share link to security whitepaper and the onboarding checklist after the call.
[05:19] [small crosstalk — 2 people speaking]
[05:23] Rajiv: technical deep dive request — can you show how KV cache hit rate responded after our change?
[05:28] Liam: we have the pre/post histograms, short version: hit rate increased 12% for long-context sessions, but for short embed bursts hit rate stayed low as expected. we'll attach graphs.
[05:40] Emily: would a table of p95/p99 by route help our SRE team?
[05:45] Liam: yes, I'll provide p50/p95/p99 by route and by model variant.
[05:50] Rajiv: and can we see a microbench for the enclave variant? we want to confirm tail-latency inside the VPC.
[05:57] Liam: yes i can run a 1-hour bench that simulates your request distribution and return both tail-latency and CPU/GPU utilization profiles.
[06:09] Dana: timeline on that?
[06:11] Liam: drop by 3/29.
[06:15] Maya: switching to roadmap — you asked about pinning models per route and having rollouts. we support model pins and can do canary rollouts with automatic fallback to a stable variant.
[06:25] Rajiv: any constraints for private pilots? e.g., we want canary, but also need the ability to rollback within 15 minutes.
[06:32] Maya: rollbacks are immediate as config flips, but permit a short in-flight token drift; operationally we give you a circuit-breaker policy and automatic fallback to the pinned stable model. we've tested rollback latencies under 30s in our staging runs.
[06:46] Emily: sweet. for the pilot, what minimal telemetry should we plan to collect?
[06:50] Sofia: at minimum: per-request latencies, per-model tokenized counts, cache hit rates, error types with traces, and cost per-route. we'll provide a recommended dashboard template.
[07:01] Tomás: finance question — what's the SLA credit if we hit >=99.9% and then drop?
[07:06] Maya: our SLA docs list tiered credits; if monthly uptime drops below the target you are eligible for pro-rated credits. we'll attach the SLA PDF.
[07:16] Rajiv: ok last piece, pilot scope: we'd like a 6-week pilot to validate cost, latency, and feature parity for our search product. timeline: kickoff week of Apr 5, run for 6 weeks, then decision.
[07:30] Sofia: noted. i'll send a Doodle for stakeholders and include security onboarding slots.
[07:36] Maya: recap — action items: 1) send per-model 30-day usage + cost variant 2) Liam bench for enclave latency 3) security docs + audit playbook 4) schedule pilot kickoff. Anything else?
[07:52] Emily: please include the embeddings quantization sample on our sample data.
[07:56] Liam: yes will run quantized embedder on your sample corpus and share quality metrics.
[08:03] Dana: thanks all, this was helpful.
[08:06] Maya: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with notes and the links.
[08:11] Meeting end.
